title.narrative: 2.1.1 Percentage or number of obsolete laws (acts and secondary legislations) repealed, removed and / or updated from the statute book by the LRC (disaggregated by topic and type of repeal) with the support of the programme.

description.narrative: This is a quantitative indicator that is meant to count the number of obsolete acts or secondary legislations that need to be repealed by the Law Reform commission, in order to update the statute book currently compiled (laws published from 1800 until 2018) and taking into account the laws published after 2018. All these laws are now published on the website: Lesotholii.org, through a support that has been provided to the OPC (see follow up indicator). However, the LRC is mandated to undertake research, repeal outdated laws or provisions and integrate remaining valid provisions in more recent or modern laws. Despite its quantitative characteristic, the indicator will enable to track the process utilised by the LRC to repeal and amend the outdated legislations and to assess which legislation has been amended or repealed therefore contributing to the principles of clarity and foreseeability of the law, necessary to contribute to the Rule of Law.

comment.narrative: The baseline has been set at 0 for July 2023 as the LRC has not started this work.

The targets for this indicator will have to be set based on the procedure guidelines and planning developed by the LRC first based on the number of laws identified for revision repeal update and or amendment for the 1st year. Then for the following years based on the listing identified and plan a percentage of 30 to 40 of legislations could be examined for repeals consultations and revision.

title.narrative: 2. Average Rule of Law and Justice score

description.narrative: This indicator reports the ranking and score assigned to Lesotho and other African countries, by the Ibrahim Index of African Governance, (IIAG) in 4 main classifications, which most relevant for the programme are Security and Rule of Law and Participation, Rights and inclusion. Each of both main categories is subdivided in 4 subcategories and sub indicators and indicates scores where 100 is the best and 0 the worst. For the Security and Rule of Law main category, Lesotho has a trend classification of bouncing back. The subcategories of Rule of Law and justice and accountability and transparency need to be mostly considered by the project.It is noted that this indicator reflects Lesothos average score and position for all the country, with only specifications on thematic sub criteria but not on geographic locations. Moreover, there are a lot of factors at work that can influence the ranking and score of the category and subindicators. The contribution by the programme to any change is therefore likely to be small. However, the analysis of the trends over a period of 10 years is interesting to look at.

comment.narrative: The baseline year set for the programme is 2022 available data was published in 2023 with an overall score 64.1 out of 100.
